**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.2.1 upgrades its managed Hibernate dependency from 6.3 to Hibernate 6.4.1.Final. The v3.2.1 GitHub release lists "Upgrade to Hibernate 6.4.1.Final #38870 as official support has been dropped for the 6.3 generation" under the "Noteworthy" section and again under "Dependency Upgrades" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1). The 3.2.x dependency-management BOM now manages the `org.hibernate.orm` group at version `6.4.1.Final` for artifacts `hibernate-ant`, `hibernate-c3p0`, `hibernate-community-dialects`, `hibernate-core`, `hibernate-envers`, `hibernate-graalvm`, `hibernate-hikaricp`, `hibernate-jcache`, `hibernate-jpamodelgen`, `hibernate-micrometer`, `hibernate-proxool`, `hibernate-spatial`, `hibernate-testing`, and `hibernate-vibur` (; the same `6.4.1.Final` values are listed for 3.2.1 at https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/3.2.1/reference/html/dependency-versions.html). This is a transitive dependency version change managed by the Spring Boot BOM; no Spring Boot class, method, annotation, or configuration property changes. A user report (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/39959, closed as invalid, labeled `status: invalid`) notes that Hibernate 6.4 dialect changes removed compatibility with some older databases (e.g., MySQL 5.7 generated-subselect queries now follow MySQL 8 syntax, referenced to `HHH-17089`), so apps against unsupported database versions may see different generated SQL or dialect behavior.

**Affects:** all applications using Hibernate ORM/JPA on Spring Boot 3.2.1 (they pull `org.hibernate.orm:*` `6.4.1.Final` transitively instead of 6.3); applications pinned to a Hibernate version explicitly, or targeting database versions whose Hibernate dialect behavior changed between 6.3 and 6.4, are at higher risk.

**Action:** none. The change is a managed dependency version bump that is applied automatically; no application code, configuration, build file, or deployment change is required. Applications must re-verify the runtime SQL generated by Hibernate and the active `org.hibernate.dialect` behavior (including database-specific query generation, e.g. subselect queries on older MySQL versions), and must re-verify any code that explicitly pins an `org.hibernate.orm` artifact to a 6.3 version against Spring Boot 3.2.1. No concrete remediation step is given in the fetched pages.

**Before/after:**
```
# Spring Boot managed Hibernate version (dependency-management BOM)
# 3.2.0: org.hibernate.orm:hibernate-core:6.3.x
# 3.2.1: org.hibernate.orm:hibernate-core:6.4.1.Final
```

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.2.0’s new nested-jar loader (using `org.springframework.boot.loader.zip.ZipContent` and the `jar:nested:` URL format) caused `META-INF` entries (such as `META-INF/persistence.xml` packaged under `BOOT-INF/classes/`) to be discovered twice, producing `Conflicting persistence unit definitions` errors (e.g. `nested:/path/to/service.jar/!BOOT-INF/classes/, file:/path/to/service.jar`). This was a regression from the classic loader. Spring Boot 3.2.1 fixes this regression ("Don't duplicate META-INF entries in nested directory jars") to align with the classic loader’s behavior, preventing the same META-INF file from being discovered twice (commit f31ffbf, [release v3.2.1](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1), [issue #38862](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38862)).

**Affects:** Applications that have `META-INF` resources (e.g. `META-INF/persistence.xml`) inside `BOOT-INF/classes/` and rely on the 3.2.0 nested jar loader (the new `org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher`).

**Action:** none (this change is a bug fix delivered by the 3.2.1 upgrade). As a temporary workaround for 3.2.0, the classic loader implementation can be used.

**Before/after:**
```gradle
tasks.named('bootJar') {
    loaderImplementation = org.springframework.boot.loader.tools.LoaderImplementation.CLASSIC
}
```

**What changed:** The property `logging.include-application-name` did not work correctly with Log4j2 because the default log pattern templates (`log4j2.xml` and `log4j2-file.xml`) used the system property `${sys:LOGGED_APPLICATION_NAME}` without a fallback default value. When `logging.include-application-name` was set to `false`, the application name system property was not set, causing the literal placeholder string `${sys:LOGGED_APPLICATION_NAME}` to appear in the console and file logs. In version 3.2.1, the placeholders in the templates were updated to `${sys:LOGGED_APPLICATION_NAME:-}`, which resolves to an empty string if the system property is not set or is empty (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38618, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/pull/38847).

**Affects:** Applications using Log4j2 that have customized logging properties in their `log4j2.xml` or `log4j2-file.xml` configurations by manually overriding `CONSOLE_LOG_PATTERN` or `FILE_LOG_PATTERN` to explicitly include `${sys:LOGGED_APPLICATION_NAME}` without the `:-` default syntax.

**Action:** required: Verify custom log patterns in `log4j2.xml` and `log4j2-file.xml`. If you manually define `CONSOLE_LOG_PATTERN` or `FILE_LOG_PATTERN` and want to include the application name, ensure you include the application name placeholder without a fallback (e.g. `${sys:LOGGED_APPLICATION_NAME}`). If you include the fallback `${sys:LOGGED_APPLICATION_NAME:-}`, it will resolve to empty when `logging.include-application-name` is `false`.

**Before/after:**
```xml
<!-- Before (v3.2.0 log4j2.xml) -->
<Property name="CONSOLE_LOG_PATTERN">%clr{%d{${sys:LOG_DATEFORMAT_PATTERN}}}{faint} %clr{${sys:LOG_LEVEL_PATTERN}} %clr{%pid}{magenta} %clr{---}{faint} %clr{${sys:LOGGED_APPLICATION_NAME}[%15.15t]}{faint} %clr{${sys:LOG_CORRELATION_PATTERN:-}}{faint}%clr{%-40.40c{1.}}{cyan} %clr{:}{faint} %m%n${sys:LOG_EXCEPTION_CONVERSION_WORD}</Property>

<!-- After (v3.2.1 log4j2.xml) -->
<Property name="CONSOLE_LOG_PATTERN">%clr{%d{${sys:LOG_DATEFORMAT_PATTERN}}}{faint} %clr{${sys:LOG_LEVEL_PATTERN}} %clr{%pid}{magenta} %clr{---}{faint} %clr{${sys:LOGGED_APPLICATION_NAME:-}[%15.15t]}{faint} %clr{${sys:LOG_CORRELATION_PATTERN:-}}{faint}%clr{%-40.40c{1.}}{cyan} %clr{:}{faint} %m%n${sys:LOG_EXCEPTION_CONVERSION_WORD}</Property>
```

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.2.0 passed `spring.pulsar.client.authentication.param.` and `spring.pulsar.admin.authentication.param.` values as a `Map<String, String>` to Pulsar's authentication API. With the Pulsar Client 3.1.0 (and later) that map-based `authentication(String pluginClassName, Map<String, String> authParams)` path is no longer supported at runtime and fails at startup with `IllegalStateException: Unable to configure Pulsar authentication` wrapping `UnsupportedAuthenticationException` / `ClassCastException` (e.g. with `org.apache.pulsar.client.impl.auth.oauth2.AuthenticationFactoryOAuth2`) (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-pulsar/issues/500). PR 38839 fixed this in `org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.pulsar.PulsarPropertiesMapper.customizeAuthentication`: the param map is now sorted into a `TreeMap`, serialized with `org.apache.pulsar.common.util.ObjectMapperFactory.create().writeValueAsString(...)`, and handed to the internal `AuthenticationConsumer.accept(String, String)` as an encoded JSON string (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/pull/38839.diff). Listed in the 3.2.1 release notes as "Pulsar authentication param properties cause IllegalStateException with Pulsar Client 3.1.0 #38839" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1).
**Affects:** Applications using Spring for Apache Pulsar auto-configuration that configure authentication via `spring.pulsar.client.authentication.plugin-class-name` together with `spring.pulsar.client.authentication.param.<name>` (or the equivalent `spring.pulsar.admin.authentication.*`) and run against Pulsar Client 3.1.0.
**Action:** none — property keys and YAML layout are unchanged; the mapper now produces the encoded string automatically. Re-verify Pulsar client and admin client start-up (OAuth2 / token / basic) succeeds.
**Before/after:**
```yaml
# spring.pulsar.client.authentication.plugin-class-name=...AuthenticationOAuth2
# spring.pulsar.client.authentication.param.issuerUrl=...
# spring.pulsar.client.authentication.param.privateKey=...
# spring.pulsar.client.authentication.param.audience=...
# (property form unchanged; autoconfig now serializes the param map to:
#   {"audience":"...","issuerUrl":"...","privateKey":"..."} )
```

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.2.0 the new loader implementation (`org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.LaunchedClassLoader`) lost `Class::getSigners()` information for signed jars listed under `requiresUnpack`: the unpacked jar was referenced with a `jar:file:/...` URL (`JarUrl.create(path.toFile())` in `JarFileArchive.getUnpackedNestedJarUrl`), so signers were no longer returned, whereas the CLASSIC loader (`LaunchedURLClassLoader`) used a `file:/...` URL and signers worked (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38833). In 3.2.1 commit `88429b6` ("Use file urls for unpacked jars") changed `org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarFileArchive` so unpacked jars use plain `file:` URLs (`path.toUri().toURL()`) rather than `jar:file:`, aligning with Spring Boot 3.1 behaviour and restoring `class.getSigners()` ().

**Affects:** Applications packaged with the new loader implementation (default in 3.2) that rely on `requiresUnpack` for signed jars whose code calls `Class::getSigners()`; such apps were broken in 3.2.0 unless they set `<loaderImplementation>CLASSIC</loaderImplementation>` on the `repackage` goal.

**Action:** required: re-verify that signature verification via `Class::getSigners()` works for `requiresUnpack` jars under the new loader; if the workaround `<loaderImplementation>CLASSIC</loaderImplementation>` was added to the `spring-boot-maven-plugin` `repackage` configuration in 3.2.0, it can be removed and the default new loader re-tested.

**Before/after:**
```java
// JarFileArchive.getUnpackedNestedJarUrl (spring-boot-loader)
// 3.2.0 (signers lost):
return JarUrl.create(path.toFile());              // -> jar:file:/.../nested.jar!/
// 3.2.1 (fixed):
return path.toUri().toURL();                       // -> file:/.../nested.jar
```

Based on the fetched pages:

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.2.0, the property `spring.testcontainers.beans.startup` (introduced in #37073) failed to enable parallel container initialization when containers were registered via `@ImportTestcontainers` (due to `ImportTestcontainersRegistrar`/`ContainerFieldsImporter` starting them sequentially during bean definition registration) or via `@Bean` methods (`TestcontainersLifecycleBeanPostProcessor`). This bug (#38831) was fixed in Spring Boot 3.2.1, restoring the expected behavior where `spring.testcontainers.beans.startup=parallel` starts `Container` beans in parallel. (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38831)

**Affects:** Applications using Spring Boot Testcontainers with `spring.testcontainers.beans.startup` set to `parallel`, where containers are defined via `@ImportTestcontainers` or `@Bean` methods.

**Action:** required: re-verify test startup times and container initialization order if `spring.testcontainers.beans.startup=parallel` is configured, as containers previously started sequentially in 3.2.0 will now start in parallel in 3.2.1.

**Before/after:**
```properties
# application.properties / application-test.properties
# Before: Ignored in 3.2.0 when using @ImportTestcontainers or @Bean containers
# After: Works correctly in 3.2.1
spring.testcontainers.beans.startup=parallel
```

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.2.1 fixes a bug where `Zip file closed exceptions` are thrown due to `StaticResourceJars` closing jars from cached connections (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1). This issue, present in 3.2.0, results in `java.lang.IllegalStateException: Zip file closed` when serving resources from nested jars, particularly when using libraries like `springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` that may interact with the resource handler and cause premature closure of jar connections (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38770, https://github.com/springdoc/springdoc-openapi/issues/2459).

**Affects:** Applications running from a nested jar (executed via `java -jar`) that use `springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` (e.g., version 2.3.0) and have disabled or non-existent endpoints that trigger static resource lookup logic in `ResourceHttpRequestHandler`.

**Action:** required: Re-verify static resource serving and Swagger/OpenAPI endpoint accessibility when running the packaged jar. Ensure `springdoc` dependencies are compatible with Spring Boot 3.2.1. If issues persist, consider updating `springdoc` to a version explicitly supporting Spring Boot 3.2.1+ or checking for related fixes in the `springdoc` project.

```java
// Example dependency from the issue report
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springdoc</groupId>
    <artifactId>springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui</artifactId>
    <version>2.3.0</version>
</dependency>
```

**What changed:** The Spring Boot 3.2.0 launcher's new `jar:nested:` URL support failed when the JAR's path contained characters like `#` (and `!` in nested entry names), throwing `java.lang.IllegalStateException: Unable to create JarFileArchive URL` / `java.net.MalformedURLException: no !/ in spec` from `org.springframework.boot.loader.net.protocol.jar.JarUrl.create` via `org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher.main` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38660). The 3.2.1 fix in `JarUrl.getJarReference` switched the file path from the decoded `file.toURI().getPath()` to the encoded `file.toURI().getRawPath().replace("!", "%21")`, so directories containing `#` or `!` are accepted (). The resulting nested URL now percent-encodes `#` as `te%23st` (). The change is listed as a bug fix in the 3.2.1 release (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1).

**Affects:** Fat JARs started via `org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher` where the JAR file's folder or file name contains reserved URL characters such as `#` or `!`.

**Action:** none

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.2.0, `SslPropertiesBundleRegistrar.registerBundles(...)` (`org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.ssl.SslPropertiesBundleRegistrar`, lines ~58-61) iterated every configured `spring.ssl.bundle.*` entry at start-up and resolved the stores eagerly, so a bundle whose keystore/trustore file did not exist failed startup with `java.io.FileNotFoundException` even when the bundle was never requested — e.g. a bundle defined in `application.yml` while `server.ssl.enabled: false` was set in `application-local.yml` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38659). 3.2.1 lists this as a bug fix, labeled `type: regression`: "FileNotFoundException is thrown eagerly from unused SSL bundles #38659", i.e. bundles that are configured but not used no longer force the underlying certificate/private-key/keystore files to be read during registration (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1).

**Affects:** Applications that define one or more `spring.ssl.bundle.pem.…` / `spring.ssl.bundle.jks.…` (or other `spring.ssl.bundle`) entries pointing at files that do not exist or whose placeholders (`${CERT_FILE_PATH}`, `${CERT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH}`) are unresolvable, and that never look up that bundle (directly via `SslBundles`, or via `server.ssl.bundle`, or other `…ssl.bundle` properties).

**Action:** none — this is a regression fix restoring 3.1-style lazy behaviour; no code, configuration or dependency changes are required. Re-verify that an application with an unused, mis-configured SSL bundle starts without `FileNotFoundException`, and that bundles which *are* referenced still fail fast if their files are missing.

**Before/after:**
```yaml
# application.yml — bundle defined but not used in the active profile
spring:
  ssl:
    bundle:
      pem:
        server-ssl-bundle:
          keystore:
            certificate: ${CERT_FILE_PATH}
            private-key: ${CERT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH}

# application-local.yml
server:
  ssl:
    enabled: false
```

**What changed:** `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionFailureAnalyzer` now accounts for the fact that missing `-parameters` compiler flag may be the cause of bean ambiguity failures. The related failure analyzer for code not compiled with `-parameters` was also updated in #38603. If parameter names are missing, the usual selection logic will fail (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38652). The `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionFailureAnalyzer` class is part of `org.springframework.boot.diagnostics` package.

**Affects:** Applications using constructor injection with multiple beans of the same type, especially when using Lombok or similar tools where parameter names may not be preserved in compiled bytecode without the `-parameters` flag.

**Action:** required: Ensure your application and dependent libraries are compiled with the `-parameters` Java compiler flag. See  for how Spring Boot ensures the `-parameters` flag is included.

**Before/after:**
No concrete code/configuration snippet available from fetched pages.

I'll stop calling tools. I have enough from the release notes and the issue body describing the fix's effect.

**What changed:** In 3.2.0, `management.tracing.enabled=false` only disabled the span-exporting/reporting beans; the propagation beans remained in place, so tracing context was still propagated over the wire (e.g. `traceparent` headers sent via HTTP) and new traces were started — a regression from pre-3.2 behavior (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38625). Fixed in 3.2.1 (commit 02347ab, "Disable propagation of traces if tracing is disabled") so that `management.tracing.enabled` now also disables trace propagation over the wire in addition to span exporting (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38641). Listed under Bug Fixes in the 3.2.1 release notes: "Traces are propagated if tracing is disabled #38641" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1).

**Affects:** Applications using tracing (Micrometer Tracing with Brave or OpenTelemetry) that set `management.tracing.enabled=false`; previously they still observed outgoing trace headers, now they will not.

**Action:** required: re-verify that any `traceparent` (or other propagation) headers you depended on are no longer emitted when `management.tracing.enabled=false`; use this property to disable both exporting and propagation rather than excluding `AutoConfiguration` via `spring.autoconfigure.exclude`.

**Before/after:**
```properties
# 3.2.0: propagation still active despite this flag
# 3.2.1: this flag now disables both span exporting and trace propagation
management.tracing.enabled=false
```

**What changed:** This is a bug fix in 3.2.1 for a 3.2.0 regression in the rewritten Uber Jar ("nested jar") loader. The new loader introduced in 3.2.0 (with URLs like `jar:nested:/dir/myjar.jar/!BOOT-INF/lib/nested.jar!/com/example/MyClass.class` replacing `jar:file:/dir/myjar.jar:BOOT-INF/lib/nested.jar!/com/example/MyClass.class`, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-3.2-Release-Notes/cc64e50682721f1c33b47273ce6e0c5ce61c16d4) used a `java.nio` file channel, which cannot be used from an interrupted thread; when a thread was interrupted (e.g. by the MongoDB driver detecting a cluster change), class loading failed with `java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: com.mongodb.event.ServerClosedEvent` ( notes "A file channel cannot be used from an interrupted thread whereas RandomAccessFile can. See #38611 for background."). Issue #38611, labeled `type: regression` and milestone 3.2.1, was closed as completed by commit `e697024` on Dec 7, 2023, and is listed in the v3.2.1 release notes under Bug Fixes (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1). The fix lives in the loader classes packaged by the build plugin, so the `spring-boot-maven-plugin` / Gradle plugin version must also be 3.2.1, not just the dependencies (a reporter confirmed fixing it only after upgrading the plugin; ).
**Affects:** Applications running as executable ("Uber") jars using the default 3.2.0 nested-jar loader (`org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher`, etc.), where classes from nested jars are loaded on threads that may be interrupted (reported with MongoDB/AWS DocumentDB cluster-change monitoring and with `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`).
**Action:** required: re-verify that the application, and especially the `spring-boot-maven-plugin` (or Spring Boot Gradle plugin), is at 3.2.1 so the fixed loader classes are repackaged into the jar; rebuilding with the new plugin is what delivers the fix. Alternatively, the 3.2 loader fallback `loaderImplementation` = `CLASSIC` restores the pre-3.2 loader (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-3.2-Release-Notes/cc64e50682721f1c33b47273ce6e0c5ce61c16d4); no code change is otherwise needed on 3.2.1.
**Before/after:**
```xml
<!-- Maven fallback documented in the 3.2 release notes if the new loader misbehaves -->
<plugin>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
  <configuration>
    <loaderImplementation>CLASSIC</loaderImplementation>
  </configuration>
</plugin>
```
```groovy
// Gradle equivalent
bootJar { loaderImplementation = org.springframework.boot.loader.tools.LoaderImplementation.CLASSIC }
```

**What changed:** Previously, failures due to missing `-parameters` compilation flags were hard to identify because the exception messages did not explicitly state that the missing parameter name information was the root cause. The `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionFailureAnalyzer` did not account for the fact that missing `-parameters` may be the cause (#38652), and `ValueObjectBinder` did not provide helpful exceptions (#38603) (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38603). Spring Boot 3.2.1 improved these diagnostics to make it clear when compilation flags are missing (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1).
**Affects:** Applications compiled without the `-parameters` flag that experience `BeanCreationException`, `NoSuchBeanDefinitionException`, or property binding errors on constructor parameters.
**Action:** required: re-verify build configuration. Ensure Java compiler arguments include `-parameters` to preserve constructor parameter names required by Spring Framework 6.1.
**Before/after:**
```java
// Before (3.2.0): Generic error without clear cause regarding '-parameters'
// After (3.2.1): Failure analyzers now explicitly identify missing '-parameters'
```

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.2.0's new loader, opening a JDK `ZipFileSystem` over a nested jar URL (e.g. `FileSystems.newFileSystem(URI.create("jar:nested:/.../app.jar/!BOOT-INF/lib/foo.jar"), Collections.emptyMap())`) failed with `java.util.zip.ZipException: read CEN tables failed`. The root cause was in `NestedByteChannel.read` (used by the `nested`/`zip:nested` NIO provider backed by `org.springframework.boot.loader.zip`): it could return only some of the bytes for a read. That is allowed by the `ByteChannel` API contract, but the JDK `ZipFileSystem` relies on all remaining bytes being returned when reading the zip central directory (CEN) tables. Commit `9a0f954` fixed `NestedByteChannel.read` to "loop until all remaining data has been read into the buffer", and shipped in 3.2.1 as bug fix #38595 (related parent regression #38592, where JobRunr-style code listing classpath directories via `FileSystemProvider` was broken) (, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38595, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1).

**Affects:** Applications or libraries (e.g. JobRunr) that open JDK NIO `ZipFileSystem`s via `FileSystems.newFileSystem`/`getFileSystem` against `jar:nested:` URLs of Spring Boot 3.2.0 uber jars; fixed purely in the loader in 3.2.1.

**Action:** none — this is a bug fix delivered in 3.2.1; applications need no code or configuration change, only re-verify that nested-jar `ZipFileSystem` access works as before 3.2.

**Before/after:**
```java
// Before 3.2.1: throws java.util.zip.ZipException: read CEN tables failed
FileSystems.newFileSystem(
    URI.create("jar:nested:/.../example-java-mag-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar/!BOOT-INF/lib/jobrunr-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar"),
    Collections.emptyMap());
```
(https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38595)

**What changed:** In 3.2.0, `management.metrics.tags` (`MetricsProperties#getTags`) was deprecated with `management.observations.key-values` as the replacement. However, `management.observations.key-values` only applies to metrics created through `Observation`s, leaving other metrics (e.g., default JVM metrics) without common tags. Issue #38583 resolved this in 3.2.1 by removing the deprecation of `management.metrics.tags`. The v3.2.1 release notes list #38583 as a bug fix under "🐞 Bug Fixes" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1). As noted in #38973, "#38583 ... did not make any functional changes, it only removed the deprecation of the property" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38973).

**Affects:** Applications that set `management.metrics.tags` in Spring Boot 3.2.0 and received deprecation warnings, or applications that migrated common tags from `management.metrics.tags` to `management.observations.key-values` and noticed that non-Observation-based metrics (e.g., JVM metrics like `process_uptime_seconds`) lost their common tags.

**Action:** none: `management.metrics.tags` is no longer deprecated in 3.2.1, so applications can continue using it without migration; if common tags are missing on non-Observation metrics after 3.2.1 upgrade, re-verify tag configuration.

**What changed:** A regression introduced in the new Spring Boot 3.2.0 zip loader (`org.springframework.boot.loader.zip`) threw `java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException` from `org.springframework.boot.loader.zip.ZipContent$Loader` (e.g. `ZipContent$Loader.load`, `ZipContent.open`) when a jar contained certain nested jars — most notably when `snowflake-jdbc` 3.14.x was a dependency — while `snowflake-jdbc` 3.13.x and Spring Boot 3.1.x were unaffected (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38572). This is a bug fix in 3.2.1, not a behaviour or API change: the fixed loader correctly parses the affected nested-zip data so no exception is thrown (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1, listed under “Bug Fixes” as “NegativeArraySizeException can be thrown from org.springframework.boot.loader.zip.ZipContent$Loader #38572”). A duplicate report (#38616) showed the same failure when running a packaged jar, `NegativeArraySizeException: -26949`, after moving from 3.1.6 to 3.2.0 (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38616).

**Affects:** Applications using Spring Boot 3.2.0 whose jar includes a nested jar (such as `snowflake-jdbc` 3.14.x) that triggers the loader bug, causing failure either at runtime (`java -jar`) or during `java -Djarmode=layertools -jar target/*.jar extract --destination target/extracted`.

**Action:** none (fixed in 3.2.1; no application code or configuration change is required beyond upgrading the version. If a workaround is needed before upgrading, downgrade the offending dependency to `snowflake-jdbc` 3.13.x or fall back to the classic loader, but neither is documented as a required step for 3.2.1.)

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.2.0 introduced the `spring.main.keep-alive` property ("Keeping the JVM alive"), which starts a non-daemon keep-alive thread. The thread was created eagerly in the constructor, so when `keep-alive: true` was set, builds using AOT processing hung indefinitely on the Gradle `processAot` step — the JVM would not exit because the keep-alive thread was running (issue #38531, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38531). In 3.2.1 this was fixed by commit `86c2f28` "Prevent keep alive thread from blocking the AOT processing": "Instead of creating the thread directly in the constructor, the thread is now created when the context is refreshed and stopped when the context is closed. As AOT processing never refreshes the context, the thread is never started and can't block the AOT processing task" (). Listed as a bug fix in the v3.2.1 release notes (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1).

**Affects:** Applications on 3.2.0 that set `spring.main.keep-alive: true` and use AOT processing / native image builds (the `processAot` build step).

**Action:** none — this is a bug fixed by upgrading to 3.2.1; `spring.main.keep-alive: true` then works with AOT builds. Re-verify that `processAot` completes with `keep-alive` enabled.

**Before/after:** no code or configuration change is required; the property `spring.main.keep-alive` is unchanged, only the internal thread lifecycle (now started on context refresh, stopped on context close, never started during AOT processing).

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.2.1, `TaskExecutionAutoConfiguration` now maps `spring.task.execution.shutdown.await-termination-period` (when `await-termination` is `true`) to `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutorBuilder#taskTerminationTimeout(Duration)`, and that in turn configures `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor#setTaskTerminationTimeout(...)` on the auto-configured `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor` used for virtual threads (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38528, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/commit/e454470, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/commit/fdbd65a). Before 3.2.1 the property was silently ignored for `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor`, so `taskTerminationTimeout` was not set and graceful termination could not wait for running tasks (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38528, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/35710).

**Affects:** Applications on Spring Boot 3.2.0 that enable virtual threads (so the auto-configured executor is `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor`) and set `spring.task.execution.shutdown.await-termination-period` (and `await-termination=true`).

**Action:** required: re-verify graceful shutdown timing of `@Async`/MVC/WebFlux async workloads, since `spring.task.execution.shutdown.await-termination-period` now actually controls `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor` termination timeout; adjust the period value if the previously-ignored setting was intentionally large.

**Before/after:**
```properties
# application.properties (unchanged key; behavior differs across versions)
spring.task.execution.shutdown.await-termination=true
spring.task.execution.shutdown.await-termination-period=30s
```

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.2.0, the rewritten nested jar loader (the new `jar:nested:` URL implementation used by `org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher`, default since 3.2 unless `loaderImplementation=CLASSIC` is set) returned `null` from `classLoader.getResource("")` for the classpath root. Spring Framework's `PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver#getResources` relies on that call to resolve the classpath root directory, so pattern lookups such as `"classpath:application-*.properties"` failed inside a repackaged jar with `java.io.FileNotFoundException: class path resource [] cannot be resolved to URL because it does not exist`, thrown from `org.springframework.core.io.ClassPathResource.getURL(ClassPathResource.java:230)` via `PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver.findPathMatchingResources` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38524). This was labelled a regression and fixed in 3.2.1, listed in the release notes as "Nested URLs return null from classLoader.getResource("") causing ClassPathResource failures #38524" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1). It worked in 3.1.x and in 3.2.x with `loaderImplementation=CLASSIC` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38524).

**Affects:** Applications packaged as executable ("uber") jars that, when run with the new 3.2 loader implementation (i.e. not `loaderImplementation=CLASSIC`), resolve classpath root URLs — e.g. `classLoader.getResource("")`, `new ClassPathResource("")`, or wildcard patterns like `classpath:application-*.properties` via `PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver` — typically before `SpringApplication#run`.

**Action:** required: upgrade restores the old behaviour; no code changes described in the sources beyond moving off 3.2.0. Applications pinned at 3.2.0 could set `loaderImplementation=CLASSIC` as a workaround; after upgrading, re-verify any classpath pattern scanning that runs from `main` or before context startup.

**Before/after:**
```
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException
	at org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.Launcher.launch(Launcher.java:91)
	at org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher.main(JarLauncher.java:58)
Caused by: java.io.FileNotFoundException: class path resource [] cannot be resolved to URL because it does not exist
	at org.springframework.core.io.ClassPathResource.getURL(ClassPathResource.java:230)
	at org.springframework.core.io.support.PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver.findPathMatchingResources(PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver.java:574)
```

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.2.0 introduced configuration properties that bind directly to Liquibase enums introduced in Liquibase 4.23+ (e.g. `liquibase.UpdateSummaryOutputEnum`), which `LiquibaseProperties` now depends on; with an older `liquibase-core` on the classpath this fails at startup ("it does not contain the liquibase.UpdateSummaryOutputEnum class upon which Spring Boot now depends"), and the discussion concluded "we should consider making a change to LiquibaseProperties so that it doesn't directly rely upon the recently introduced Liquibase enums" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38522). Separately, the reported symptom in the issue — a checksum validation error during rollback when a Liquibase parameter is used in a SQL changelog with `test-rollback-on-update: true` — was judged not to be a Spring Boot regression: "The same problem occurs with Spring Boot 3.1.6 if you use Liquibase 4.24.0 (the default version in Spring Boot 3.2) or 4.25.0" and users were asked to report it to the Liquibase team (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38522). The issue was fixed and shipped in 3.2.1 under the Bug Fixes list entry "Spring Boot 3.2 is not compatible with older versions of Liquibase #38522" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.2.1).

**Affects:** Applications that use Liquibase (`liquibase-core`) with a version older than the managed Liquibase 4.24.0 while relying on the 3.2 `spring.liquibase.*` summary/UI properties, and applications using `spring.liquibase.test-rollback-on-update=true` with Liquibase parameters in SQL changelogs (the latter symptom is a Liquibase-side behaviour, reproducible on 3.1.6 with Liquibase 4.24.0/4.25.0).

**Action:** required: re-verify Liquibase startup and rollback behaviour on 3.2.1 (the `LiquibaseProperties`/`LiquibaseAutoConfiguration` enum coupling was fixed for this milestone); if you pinned an older `org.liquibase:liquibase-core` over Boot's managed version, re-verify that the `spring.liquibase.*` summary options still bind; for the `test-rollback-on-update` checksum error with SQL-changelog parameters, the Spring Boot team directed this to Liquibase, so verify the checksum behaviour with the Liquibase version you use rather than changing Spring Boot code.

**Before/after:**

```properties
#  (demo of the reported failure)
# application.properties
# liquibase parameter used by db/changelog/testWithParams.sql
spring.liquibase.test-rollback-on-update=true
```
